messages:
michael: Heads-up — bench flaked on the new LLM-3 checkpoint format when ingested into the smoke runner. I'm thinking we need a small manifest + fingerprint layer for checkpoint handoff so bench/runtime don't need bespoke parsers. Repro: `ingest --check model.tar.gz` -> failing on missing kv_index.
tara: Can you paste the failing lines?
michael: ```
ERROR ingest: failed to open kv_index: key not found in archive
trace: model.tar.gz -> /kv_index (expected kv_layout=v2)
```
liam: Sounds like a kernel/layout mismatch. Some runtimes expect KV layout v2; the checkpoint we got is v1 + quant metadata. Options: (1) standard manifest that declares layout + hashes, (2) translation step during intake (CPU heavy), (3) runtime shim that maps v1->v2 on the fly.
sylvie: Manifest + fingerprint is my vote. Also include a smokecache checksum so smoke runs can reuse prefix caches across equivalent checkpoints. Minimal manifest fields: `seqlen_hist`, `kv_layout`, `quant_params`, `artifact_hash`.
michael: Example manifest I sketched:```json
{
  "model_name": "llm-3x",
  "artifact_hash": "sha256:...",
  "kv_layout": "v2",
  "seqlen_hist": "[1, 8, 16, 512]",
  "quant_params": { "bits": 8, "scheme": "q4_0" },
  "sub_artifacts": [{ "path": "kv_index", "hash": "sha256:..." }]
}
```
tara: Tradeoffs: manifests centralize compatibility but introduce onboarding churn — owners need to keep manifests in sync. We should mandate generation in CI or intake. Also need sub-artifact granular hashes to allow partial caches.
liam: I lean to generating manifests in intake (automated) and requiring model infra to validate before admission. Runtime should early-reject incompatible binaries with clear errors (e.g., "runtime: unsupported kv_stride=3"). We should document kernel flags (`kv_stride`, `chunked_kv`) that cause rejects vs those we can translate.
benchbot: bench-results: smoke-run 1749876545 — 1 failure: KV layout mismatch. 3 warmup passes OK. details: https://bench.redwood.example/runs/1749876545 :eyes:
michael: Ok next steps: I'll draft a short RFC that defines the manifest schema, a validator (intake), and an optional translation step. Who can review? @tara @liam
tara: I'll review the schema and take ownership of the validator implementation.
sylvie: I'll sketch how smokecache should index artifacts by manifest fields and propose migration plan for existing cached prefixes.
liam: I'll implement runtime reject logic + fallback shim spec (if we decide translation is worth it).
michael: I'll open a PR with proto + example artifacts and a tiny reference generator. Expecting to push later today. :thumbsup:
opsbot: Reminder scheduled: follow-up sync (eng-ml) tomorrow 09:30 to align on RFC comments.
michael: Thanks all — syncing in the RFC thread once PR is up.
